result.topic_en: Euler finishes showing that 64013 is prime. He then tests whether N = 999601 = 840·34² + 169² can be written as 840xx + yy in more than one way, by repeatedly subtracting 840·(2x−1). The table finds a second representation, with y = 979 and x = 7.

§. 58. His circa evolutionem numerorum in forma $40aa + 13bb$ contentorum expeditis, praestabit usum majorum numerorum idoneorum exemplo illustrasse. Consideretur numerus $N = 999601 = 840 \cdot 34^2 + 169^2$, et examinetur, utrum hic numerus propositus plus uno modo in forma idonea $840xx + yy$ [?] contineatur, id quod sine pluris ambagibus sequenti modo satis commode fieri licet.

§. 59. Cum debeat esse $999601 - 840xx = yy$, ipsi $x$ successive tribuantur numeri naturales et numeri S a proposito subtrahendi cum suis differentiis erunt

$x$ | S | Diff.
0 | 0 | $1 \cdot 840$
1 | $1 \cdot 840$ | $3 \cdot 840$
2 | $4 \cdot 840$ | $5 \cdot 840$
3 | $9 \cdot 840$ | $7 \cdot 840$
4 | $16 \cdot 840$ | etc.
etc. | etc. |

Loco S jam continuo subtrahantur differentiae augmento 1680 crescentes, quae subtractiones continuae sequenti modo instituantur.

items.english: Since no square results from this, we conclude that the number 64013 is prime.

items.quote: Consideretur numerus $N = 999601 = 840 \cdot 34^2 + 169^2$, et examinetur, utrum hic numerus propositus plus uno modo in forma idonea $840xx + yy$ [?] contineatur
items.english: Consider the number N = 999601 = 840·34² + 169², and examine whether this proposed number is contained in the idoneal form 840xx + yy in more than one way.

items.quote:
Numerus igitur propositus duplici modo in forma idonea $840xx + yy$ continetur, ideoque non

items.english: The proposed number is therefore contained in the idoneal form 840xx + yy in two ways, and hence is not [prime].
